==Problem==
The <math>5</math>-digit number <math>\underline{2}</math> <math>\underline{0}</math> <math>\underline{1}</math> <math>\underline{8}</math> <math>\underline{U}</math> is divisible by <math>9</math>. What is the remainder when this number is divided by <math>8</math>?

<math>\textbf{(A) }1\qquad\textbf{(B) }3\qquad\textbf{(C) }5\qquad\textbf{(D) }6\qquad\textbf{(E) }7</math>

==Solution==

We use the property that the digits of a number must sum to a multiple of <imath>9</imath> if it are divisible by <imath>9</imath>. This means <imath>2+0+1+8+U</imath> must be divisible by <imath>9</imath>. The only possible value for <imath>U</imath> then must be <imath>7</imath>. Since we are looking for the remainder when divided by <imath>8</imath>, we can ignore the thousands. The remainder when <imath>187</imath> is divided by <imath>8</imath> is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }3}</imath>.

If you got stuck on this problem, refer to AOPS Number Theory. You're smart.

-InterstellerApex, Nivaar

Quick addon:

<imath>187-160</imath> (<imath>8 \times 20</imath>)<imath>=27</imath>. <imath>27-24</imath> (<imath>8 \times 3</imath>)=<imath>3</imath>. Therefore, the answer is <imath>\boxed{\textbf{(B) }3}</imath>.
